To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) farm households in the case study areas have more spatially-concentrate transactions in the case of NE Scotland, while in Podlaski transactions are more spatially-dispersed and take place closer to the farm; 2) in both case study areas, the majority of input purchases take place in the locality; 3) the majority of output sales are made to distant markets; and 4) the majority of off-farm employment takes place in the local area.

the economic integration of farm household transactions is highly context dependent and that the spatial distribution of transactions is influenced by the economic geography of a region, farm household attachment to their locality, and the supply side factors of the agri-food system.

farm households in both study areas make a significant contribution to their local economy, but the extent and nature of this contribution is influenced by a variety of factors, including farm size, the local economic context and farmer attitudes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the local economic integration and contribution of farm households.
how the local economic benefits from farming are measured and how this might be used to inform future policy development and implementation.
understanding the local economic contribution of farm households and the factors that influence the spatial pattern of their transactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the concept of the “local” is highly context dependent.
the local economy of farm households in the case study areas is highly integrated, with a high proportion of transactions taking place in the locality.
the local economic contribution of farm households is highly context specific and dependent on the local economic and social structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
local economic integration of the farm households in the two areas is not a function of farm size but rather of the economic geography of each area.
the local economic integration (LEI) of farm households is a complex and dynamic process which is influenced by a range of factors, some of which are exogenous to the farm household.
farm households are more integrated into their local economies than previously thought but that the nature of their transactions is influenced by local economic conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local economic contribution of farm households is highly context specific and depends on the nature of the agri-food system in the area under analysis and on farm household characteristics.
the local economic impact of farm households varies considerably across Europe and is influenced by the economic geography of a region.

the local economic contribution of farm households is not straightforward to measure and depends on a number of factors, including farm size, the economic geography of an area and the structure of the agri-food system.
